clue.text: Express disapproval in the end ?

definitions.meaning: to protest or raise a complaint against something
an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'the end justifies the means'

explanation.definitionFit: To protest is to raise an objection; and a goal or purpose, one's aim, is also a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Sexton, poet or admiral

definitions.meaning: Sexton ..., the fictional detective of British story papers
William ..., the English Romantic poet and artist
Robert ..., the 17th-century English naval commander

explanation.walkthrough: Sexton Blake is a British pulp-fiction detective; 'Sexton' looks like a church officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the pulp detective Sexton, the visionary poet William, and Cromwell's naval commander Robert.

clue.text: Meant site to be adapted for a café

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The location was intended to become a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be adapted' reworks MEANT SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or bistro, the kind of place serving drinks and snacks.

clue.text: Perhaps Indians reduce figure at meeting demanding a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to slim is to reduce one's figure
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dieters meeting demand a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding a rise' turns SLIM AT upwards; Tamils are a people of southern India and Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamils are an ethnic group largely from southern India, so they are an example of Indians.

clue.text: Security device of local key-maker

indicators.note: the key-maker of the surface becomes a signal that the letters of the words before it are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lock produced by the neighbourhood locksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key-maker' reads as a locksmith, but 'maker' alone is the anagram signal working on LOCAL KEY; the Yale is a well-known cylinder lock, named after its American inventor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yale is a brand of pin-tumbler lock fitted to doors for protection against intruders.

clue.text: Constantly giving oneself away before signing?

definitions.text: Constantly giving oneself away before signing?

parts.words: Constantly giving oneself away before signing?
parts.note: a formal letter's closing words, read as loyally handing oneself over to the reader just before the signature

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constantly' is the faithful part and 'giving oneself away' the belonging-to-you part of a standard letter sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal valediction placed before a signature at the end of a letter to an unnamed recipient.

clue.text: They wrong about everyone under fifty in a deadly way

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places one piece below the other

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other
wrong signals the letters of the word they in a bad order

parts.note: taken as written
all means everyone

explanation.surface: People who mistreat all the under-fifties in a fatal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes the anagram ETHY, 'about' wraps it round the second piece, and 'under' sets everything beneath fifty, since this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatally, in a manner causing death, is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: Bar that gives rise to merrymaking

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to revel is to make merry; revelry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub; it is a metal rod for prising.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowbar or rigid rod used to prise or lift is this tool.

clue.text: Captain's capital restores replacement on the mast

indicators.note: a capital is a head letter, so the first letter of the word is taken
this word means the letters it governs are mixed up, so they are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship's master's chief city restores a substitute for the mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' takes C from Captain's, and 'replacement' reworks RESTORES into ROSSTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosstrees are horizontal timbers fixed near the top of a ship's mast to spread the rigging.

clue.text: So many abroad have a horse or the equivalent

parts.note: the French for 'so much' or 'so many' is tant
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A foreigner with many horses, or something just as good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you to translate 'So many' into French, giving TANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tantamount to another thing amounts to the same, so the two are as good as identical.

clue.text: Little book about one musical instrument

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: VOL is the short form of volume, a book
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A small book about a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the abbreviation VOL for volume rather than a short book; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The viol is a bowed string instrument of the Renaissance, ancestor of the modern string family.

clue.text: They're the basis of knotty: calculations

definitions.text: They're the basis of knotty: calculations

parts.words: They're the basis of knotty: calculations
parts.note: knotty here means measured in knots, the nautical speed unit based on distance at sea per hour, not difficult

explanation.walkthrough: A knot is one nautical mile per hour, so speed calculations at sea are based on that unit of distance; 'knotty' looks like 'tricky'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical miles, the units of distance over water, underlie the knot as a measure of a ship's speed.

clue.text: Stop precedes the sentence ?

definitions.meaning: to halt or check something
a criminal is detained by police long before the judge passes sentence

explanation.definitionFit: To halt is one sense; police detention is the other, coming before trial and sentencing.

clue.text: This school back might be played ?

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a musical note is something that might be played

explanation.surface: Back play at a famous school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the famous English public school near Windsor; 'back' reverses NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a well-known English boarding school for boys.

clue.text: Collection made before the marriage service

definitions.text: Collection made before the marriage service

parts.words: Collection made before the marriage service
parts.note: not a church collection but the bride's assembled clothes and linen gathered for the wedding

explanation.walkthrough: 'Collection' looks like the church plate, but it is a bride's gathered outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's prepared wardrobe of clothes and household linen for married life.

clue.text: Attempt to fill in really unusual symbolic tale

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, filling its middle
unusual signals the letters of the following word in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: An effort to fill out a truly odd fable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters to give ALLERY, and 'to fill in' sets the attempt inside that run.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable or fable whose characters and events stand for deeper moral ideas is this kind of narrative.

clue.text: How Pershing acted, for the most part ?

definitions.meaning: John Pershing was the US Army general commanding American forces in France in World War I
usually, in most cases

explanation.walkthrough: Pershing acted as a general, so he behaved 'general-ly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Usually, in most cases; and read as 'like a general', the way the US commander Pershing behaved.

clue.text: Leaders by another name could be bounders

definitions.meaning: heads of teams or ships
bounders here are skippers, those who skip or jump

explanation.walkthrough: 'by another name' points to skippers, the alternative word for team leaders, which also means things that skip or bound.
explanation.definitionFit: Team heads are called skippers, and skippers are also leapers, so the word fits both.

clue.text: Agreement followed auction ?

definitions.meaning: a binding deal between parties
in bridge the bidding, called the auction, settles the final bid that declarer must make

explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the bidding stage is called the auction, and the final bid is the term for what follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is a binding pact; and in bridge the final bid that the bidding establishes has the same name.

clue.text: He's. one unusually inexperienced driver

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of the word one in a different order

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Somebody who is strangely a novice motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' reworks ONE into NOE; L is for a learner driver, from the L-plates such drivers display in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a man's given name, so a male person, 'he', could have it.

clue.text: Fishermen's belongings, and many others

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
anglers own reels for their lines

explanation.surface: Gear owned by anglers and plenty of other people.
explanation.walkthrough: C for a hundred stands for 'many' before REELS, another piece of anglers' kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicker baskets used by fishermen to hold their catch.

clue.text: It might give us higher standing, like money

definitions.text: It might give us higher standing

parts.note: as can mean like, as in 'dressed as a pirate'
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: Wealth may raise our social status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher standing' suggests status, but read literally it is a climb up.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb or rise takes us to a loftier position, so it gives us a higher place to stand.

clue.text: Warm bit 'at the end of a month ?

definitions.meaning: a glowing fragment left in a dying fire

definitions.text: at the end of a month
definitions.meaning: the closing letters of September, November and December

explanation.walkthrough: Four months end with these five letters, so the second reading is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing coal from a fire; and the closing letters of September, November and December.

clue.text: In favour of having a lock on the stronghold.

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in 'all those for the motion'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A supporter of putting a lock on the castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door fastening; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified building such as a castle or citadel is a strong defensive place.

clue.text: These normally include a foreign title

indicators.note: include means the letters sit inside the words before it

explanation.surface: These ordinarily feature an overseas honorific.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' finds the letters across thESE NORmally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish form of address for a man, equivalent to Mr or sir.

clue.text: Little boy growing up ?

definitions.meaning: a short form of the boy's name Herbert
a plant growing up from the ground

explanation.walkthrough: Herb is a pet form of Herbert; a herb is also a plant, something growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the name Herbert; and also a green leafy plant that grows.

clue.text: Resentment, calls, for treatment, perhaps

definitions.meaning: bitterness or hostility towards someone
read literally, feeling sick, which may need a doctor

explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or bitterness; read literally it is feeling unwell, which might need medical care.

clue.text: Woolly kind of cow

definitions.meaning: a knitted woollen sweater, the kind worn by Channel Island fishermen
a breed of dairy cattle from one of the Channel Islands

explanation.walkthrough: A woolly is a knitted pullover in British speech; the Channel Islands give their names to both a sweater and a cattle breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick knitted fisherman's jumper; and a dairy cattle breed, both named after one of the Channel Islands.

clue.text: People talking of a detective writer

definitions.meaning: those who say things
Dorothy L. ..., creator of Lord Peter Wimsey

explanation.definitionFit: Those who utter words; and Dorothy L. Sayers, the English crime novelist who created Lord Peter Wimsey.
